episode.title: Finding the Source of Truth — Agent Day 2

content.summary_short: Learn how to verify what is true inside AeroVista — authority ladder, truth labels, source checks, conflict protocol, evidence packets, and confidential-source discipline.
content.summary_long: Agent Day 2 teaches verification before action. Byte walks through why source of truth matters in a multi-layer ecosystem, the seven-rung Authority Ladder, five truth labels, the six-step Source Check Method, conflict handling, evidence packets, and legal/confidential reporting rules. Completion requires Day 2 gate acknowledgment, segment pass, quiz, and a practical Source-of-Truth Drill with conflict note.
content.key_line: Before you act, know what you are trusting.
content.start_here: Complete the Day 2 gate, listen or read all segments, pass the verification check, then submit your Source-of-Truth Drill on a real object you are checking.
content.tone: Clear, operational, slightly cinematic — less mythic than Day 1

sections.title: Cold Open
paragraphs: Yesterday, you entered AeroVista. Today, you learn how not to get tricked by it — not because AeroVista is dishonest, but because living systems generate layers.
If you treat every piece of information as equal, you will make a confident mess. AeroVista needs agents who tell reference, memory, evidence, authority, and reality apart.
Today's lesson: before you act, know what you are trusting.

sections.title: Why Source of Truth Matters
paragraphs: The same topic can appear in plans, handoffs, registries, live endpoints, legal docs, and founder notes.
Your job is not to memorize everything — it is to verify.
An AeroVista agent reports what they found, what they trust, what conflicts, the risk, and the next safe action.

sections.title: The Authority Ladder
paragraphs: Seven rungs: human instruction, live reality, registry/release, handoff/EOD, documentation, memory, external research.
Climb the ladder for the decision at hand — not every rung exists for every task.
Registered does not mean live. Memory guides search — it does not replace verification.

sections.title: The Five Truth Labels
paragraphs: Verified, Reported, Inferred, Unknown, Conflicting — use them in every important report.
Do not quietly upgrade reported into verified.
Conflicts are progress signals when surfaced clearly.

sections.title: The Source Check Method
paragraphs: Name the object. Name the decision. Find highest authority. Check staleness. Check scope.
Report: I checked, I found, I trust, I do not trust yet, the conflict is, the risk is, the next safe action is.

sections.title: Handling Conflicting Sources
paragraphs: Do not average sources or hide contradictions.
Conflict Protocol: name sources, name conflict, rank authority, safe interim decision, leave a conflict note.

sections.title: The Evidence Packet
paragraphs: Claim, evidence, source type, confidence, risk if wrong, one next action.
Judgment matters — include what breaks if you are wrong.

sections.title: Legal and Confidential Sources
paragraphs: Use confidential sources to decide — do not expose them casually.
Summarize only what is necessary. Escalate when legal, access, or ownership is unclear.

sections.title: Closing
paragraphs: Day 2 is when you stop being a narrator and start becoming an operator.
Tomorrow: Day 3 — From Signal to Action, how AVCC thinks.
Find the source. Then move.

day2_gate.title: Day 2 Gate — Verification Commitment
items: I completed Agent Day 1 (The First Door) or received equivalent operator briefing on operating law and trust.
I understand Day 2 is about verification and authority ranking — not memorizing every document in the ecosystem.
I will label claims as Verified, Reported, Inferred, Unknown, or Conflicting — and never upgrade silently.
I will surface conflicting sources instead of averaging them or picking the nicest-sounding answer.
I will protect confidential sources in public outputs while using them for safe internal decisions.

prove.title: Source-of-Truth Drill + Conflict Note
prove.description: Demonstrate you can rank sources and report uncertainty on a real check — not listen-and-leave.

fields.label: 1. Object being checked (system, doc, release, role, asset…)
2. Decision that depends on it (ship, grant access, update docs, escalate…)
3. Sources found (up to five — label each: live, registry, handoff, doc, memory, operator, legal, external)
5. Truth label (Verified / Reported / Inferred / Unknown / Conflicting)
6. Conflict check — if sources disagree: Source A says / Source B says / conflict / risk if ignored (or N/A)
9. Handoff note for the next agent

questions.q: A document says a service is active, but the live health check fails. You should treat the service as:
choices: Down until live reality proves otherwise
questions.explain: Live system reality beats stale documentation for operational state.

questions.q: Registry marks a release as registered. That means:
choices: It is live and healthy for all users
It is recorded in registry — not automatically live

questions.q: A handoff says E2E passed but you have not checked logs yourself. Best label:
questions.explain: Reported is honest — do not upgrade without proof.

questions.q: Step one of the Source Check Method is:
choices: Name the object you are checking

questions.q: When two authoritative sources disagree, you should:
choices: Surface the conflict and rank authority

questions.q: Confidential internal sources used for a decision should be:
choices: Pasted into public outputs for transparency
Used to decide safely but protected in public reporting
questions.explain: Use the source. Protect the source.

lesson.objective: Verify before acting — climb the authority ladder, label truth honestly, run source checks, surface conflicts, and leave an evidence packet.
lesson.why_it_matters: Beautifully written chaos machines cite random docs as law; Day 2 installs the verification habit that keeps agents trustworthy inside AeroVista.
lesson.apply: Complete gate, all segments, quiz, and Source-of-Truth Drill on a real object.
lesson.advance: Unlock From Signal to Action (Day 3) when sot_prove is complete.
